extension.summary: Friendly TV live channels, guide and on-demand for Kodi
extension.description:
Watch the live channel lineup, the programme guide and the on-demand catalogue from your own Friendly TV subscription, playing back through InputStream Adaptive with Widevine DRM.
Friendly TV runs on Revlet, and this addon speaks the same private endpoints as the web player at watch.frndlytv.com. Sign in with the email address and password you already use.
Features: * Live TV: every channel in your lineup, each showing what is on right now * Guide: a day of schedule per channel * Search across the channel lineup and the next twelve hours of guide * Record an episode or a whole series, and stop or delete a recording * The service's own Home, Movies, TV and My Stuff pages * Widevine playback through InputStream Adaptive, with no licence proxy -- Friendly TV's licence server speaks raw Widevine, so Kodi talks to it directly * Concurrent-stream slots are released when playback stops, so the account does not lock itself out * Optional IPTV Manager integration, putting the lineup and guide in Kodi's own TV section
Your subscription, your account, your lineup. Nothing is proxied through a third party.
extension.disclaimer: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Friendly Technologies or Frndly TV. This addon uses private, undocumented endpoints; use it with your own subscription.
extension.news: 2026.9.1 - First release - Signing in works again. Friendly TV asks which device is asking, the addon answered with the number an early capture used, and the service has since started refusing that one outright -- an empty HTTP 403, which surfaced as "issued no session id" and left no way in. A capture of a browser signing in from scratch names the number it uses now, which is the same one the addon already sends when it asks for a stream. - Signed out, the menu offers signing in and nothing else. Live TV, the guide, search and the rest need an account, and listing them was offering folders that could only fail. - Sign in and sign out no longer end in "Error getting plugin://". They are listed as folders, so Kodi calls them expecting a listing, and telling it there was none is exactly what that message reports. Both now draw the menu over the one being looked at, which after signing in is what is wanted anyway. A guide row for something not yet on the air was the same shape and is fixed with it. - A row opens in full rather than at whatever the page embedded. Every row names where the rest of it lives, in one of two shapes, and the addon follows the one the service's own page endpoint opens. The other is a carousel, which no capture ever asks for on its own, so it is left alone rather than guessed at. - A Coming Soon title says when it airs, and on which channel. The card carries it, worded by the service and in its timezone, so a badge that raised the obvious question now answers it. The field it lives in holds a bare id on most other cards, so it is read only where it is shaped like a date, and one card that puts it somewhere else entirely is read too. - A listing no longer fails on a row that is not shaped like a row. The service's "data" list is general purpose and not everything in it is a pane. - A Coming Soon title is no longer offered to the player. The service lists these and then refuses them, so Kodi was trying, failing, and logging "skipping unplayable item" once per attempt -- and a season of them takes several tries to find one that plays. They still appear in their place in the season, badged, and selecting one says what it is. - Stopping a video says so properly. Friendly TV has an event for it and no capture had ever caught one, so the addon sent a final position instead rather than invent a code; leaving a video with the back button turns out to send it, with the player back to idle and the position it reached. - Badges are actually visible now. They were being written into the row's label and then painted over: Kodi draws the info tag's title on top of the label it was given, and for an episode the addon set that title a second time from the episode's own name. So every badge computed on a season of episodes -- which is where "Coming Soon" lives -- was correct, written, and never seen. - A Trending folder, holding the three carousels the service's own search screen opens with: Trending Movies, Trending TV Shows and Trending Searches, twenty-five titles apiece. Their names and descriptions are the service's, not ones invented here. - Add-Ons is a top-level folder now rather than one row of Home. It was being skipped from the menu the service itself provides, which left it reachable only by scrolling Home; it is a page like any other, so it sits with Movies and TV, and the row that duplicated it is off Home. - A badge stays on the row it decorates. It was going into the url as well, so the player was told it was playing "A New Beginning [COLOR gold](+ Add-On)[/COLOR]", markup and all. - A listing that does not filter says why. The account's packages decide what is hidden, and when they cannot be read nothing is -- which looked exactly like a listing with nothing to hide, so the same row filtered once and not the next time with no way to tell which had happened. - Searching for a channel no longer risks losing MeTV. Friendly TV marks a card as a network whether the channel is an add-on or part of the plan, and MeTV, MeTV+ and MeTV Toons all carry that marking with pages of their own, so hiding on it alone would have taken them out of a search for "metv". A channel counts as an add-on only where the service names it as one. - The Add-ons folder lists only the channels the account actually has, unless the setting says otherwise. Friendly TV sells six of them -- Hallmark+, UP Faith & Family, Great American Pure Flix, Lifetime Movie Club, A&E Crime Central and HISTORY Vault -- and its own page lists all six whether they are paid for or not. Which ones are paid for is stated outright by the account's packages, so this is exact rather than inferred: a package says for itself that it is an add-on, which matters because the list of add-ons on offer drops one the moment it is bought. - Titles on a channel the account does not pay for are left out of listings, whatever else it pays for. One search settles what the "+ Add-On" badge means: searching "good witch" while subscribed to one add-on and not another answers with eleven titles at once -- six from a channel in the plan and five from a channel that is not, and only the five are badged. In the same session the subscribed channel's own films come back unbadged, the film that had refused to play among them. The badge says "you cannot watch this", not "this is add-on content". - Cards wear the badge the service gave them -- "On Now", "Coming Soon", "New Episodes", "Expires in 24 hours", "+ Add-On" -- on films and shows alike. Kodi has nowhere to draw a badge, so it goes in the label, in the service's own words rather than any invented here. - "Coming Soon" matters most of the six: those episodes are listed and then refused, with a message that reads like a fault -- "The content provider has restricted this program from being available On Demand." Thirty-nine of the forty-seven episodes of one captured series are Coming Soon, so finding one that plays took several tries. - Titles that need an add-on subscription are left out of listings, and a setting brings them back. The card says so itself, so nothing has to be fetched to know: "+ Add-On" is the one badge in the whole capture that carries a redirect-to-payment flag, and it carries it on every card it is on. The flag is what is read, not the wording. - A film on a channel the subscription does not include says so, instead of "Friendly TV's page for this offers nothing to play". Those titles have a full page -- synopsis, cast, artwork -- with a subscribe button where the play button would be, which read as a page with nothing on it. The offer is repeated in the service's own words, because that is the only thing that knows what it is. - Playback reports are no longer refused. The POST carries two form fields and only one was being sent; the service said so plainly once it was asked to. The missing one is a constant in the web player's own configuration, not a secret and not per-account. - The device an event came from is described by Python rather than by Kodi's info labels, which answer "Busy" when they are not ready yet and duly sent a machine whose operating system was "Busy". - What you watch in Kodi now reaches Continue Watching, and remembers where you left off. That row is written by whatever is playing, and this addon was writing nothing: the web player posts player state and position throughout playback, to a host that is not the API, and the addon posted none of it. So the row was fed only by Friendly TV's own apps, and a film watched here left no trace -- which is why Movies had a Continue Watching row with nothing in it. Only the event types the capture shows the meaning of are sent; the two it does not are left alone, and stopping sends a final position rather than an invented "stopped". Under Playback, and it can be turned off. - Opening a section the page had not filled in no longer fails with an error and an empty folder. Those come from a different endpoint, and it answers with a bare list -- one element per section code asked for, in which "section" is the code as a plain string -- where a page answers with an object whose "section" holds the info, the data and the controls under it. Read as a page it raised before it read anything. - The log no longer claims playback began 106 hours into a fifty minute film. The stream slot is claimed the moment Kodi says it is playing, which is before the demuxer has settled, and a multi-period manifest answered for its position with a number the running time could not contain. The player is now asked again until its answer fits, and told so in the log if it never does. - A film played the wrong stream entirely. The service answers with one entry per DRM system -- Widevine and PlayReady as DASH, FairPlay as HLS -- and the addon took whichever came first. With FairPlay first that gave Kodi an HLS manifest encrypted for Apple while telling it the key system was Widevine, which ISA reports as "Unhandled encrypted stream": the same words a missing key system produces, so it read like a DRM fault rather than the wrong file. The Widevine entry is now chosen by name, a DASH manifest is preferred, and an answer with no Widevine in it says so instead of being played anyway. - The stream request now carries the provider-profile id exactly where the web player was captured carrying it -- live channels and guide airings, not on-demand titles -- rather than on everything. - Video quality is a setting, and it no longer opens at the worst copy the service has. Friendly TV offers 288p, 360p, 432p and 720p and nothing higher, all four in one adaptive set in all 21 periods of an ad-inserted film, so nothing about the stream forced the choice. InputStream Adaptive made it: its default chooser skips any rendition above 90% of its estimated bandwidth, and it seeds that estimate from the speed of the manifest download -- a 120 KB file over a connection it has just opened, handshake time included. Between roughly 0.75 and 0.91 Mbit/s of estimate, 288p is the only rendition left standing. The addon now asks for the best rendition that fits and holds it, which for this service means 720p. - Playback on Kodi 21 is fixed. The DRM configuration was being written in the form only InputStream Adaptive 22.1.5 and newer reads, and ISA 21 does not warn about that -- it ignores the property and then refuses the stream with "InitializePeriod: Unhandled encrypted stream". The form is now chosen by the installed ISA version, and the log says which one went out. - Home shows its real rows. Friendly TV assembles that one screen from two endpoints, and the obvious one carries only the Live Now row, so Home was a single row of live channels. The rest come from the carousel endpoint, paged behind a cursor. - Search is Friendly TV's own catalogue search, paged, now that a capture reached the endpoint. Results mix pages to open with episodes that play, and each is routed by what it is. Shows, Movies and Channels filters sit at the top of the first page. - A film's page is no longer empty. Films and series are not built from the section shape the rest of the service uses: what plays them is a button in the page's content pane, and a film has nothing else on it at all. - A search that matches nothing says so instead of reporting an error. The search API answers no-matches with status false and a 404, which is a refusal in the protocol's terms and an empty list in anyone else's. - Search shows every result at once rather than a chain of "Next page" folders. It walks the pages itself, which for the totals this service returns is three to five requests. - A film plays in one click. Its card points at a page, but that page holds a single play button and nothing else, so the page is fetched and the button followed rather than listed as a folder to open. A series stays a folder, because it really does have seasons under it. - Shows, films and episodes are labelled as such for Kodi, so skins lay them out as shows and films instead of anonymous folders, and an episode carries its own name and its season and episode numbers. - Descriptions, cast, director, year and certificate now reach Kodi's own Information dialog. Friendly TV sends none of that with a listing -- it is empty on all but a handful of the 8191 cards captured, and lives only on each title's page -- so those pages are fetched for a listing's films and shows on a small pool of threads. One request per title is a real cost, so it is a setting with a cap, under Listings. - Picking the programme on the air in the guide asks whether to play live or start it over. Those turn out to be two different paths to the same endpoint rather than two kinds of request: the channel's gives the live edge, the programme's own is answered with the programme from its start. - Add to and remove from Favourites, on anything with a path -- films, shows, channels and guide airings alike. Only the verb that applies is offered, because the cards carry whether they are already in. These are Friendly TV's My Stuff, so they appear there and in its own apps. - "Remove from Continue Watching" on any part-watched title. The row is made of cards carrying a resume position, so no flag is needed to know which ones qualify, and the call is keyed by the card's own id and content type. - A listing no longer fails whole because of one row Kodi would not accept, and an unexpected error no longer surfaces as Kodi's bare "Error getting plugin://..." with nothing about the cause. The row is skipped and named, or the traceback is logged and the folder opens empty with a message. - Favouriting a film from a listing and coming back no longer offers to add it again. A listing card's isFavourite does not keep up with a change -- a live channel's and a guide airing's do -- but the title's own page states it, and that page is already being fetched for the synopsis, so the authoritative answer was free and was simply not being used. - Leaving a live channel no longer marks it watched. A channel's card carries the running time of whatever is on it, and handing Kodi that as a duration made a channel look like a finite video, so stopping partway through counted as finishing it. A channel is never finished. - Start Over now opens at the beginning of the programme's window rather than at the live edge. Asked for a programme still on the air, the service answers with a live manifest -- not the VOD asset it returns once the programme has finished -- and a live manifest opens where the channel is. - The guide marks what is already set to record, and offers only the context-menu entry that applies rather than both. The flag is on no schedule row anywhere, so it comes from a second endpoint that answers for a whole batch of channels at once -- which is what makes it affordable. It is a membership set and nothing more: every "info" object in every captured response is empty, and the web player treats it the same way. - An "Active streams" entry showing what the account has playing anywhere, from the concurrency counter's own view. Every capture caught that endpoint empty, so the count is trustworthy and the shape of an entry is not; entries are rendered from whatever fields they turn out to carry. - Searching by genre and by person, which turned out to need no new endpoint: the search the addon already had ranks over titles, people and genre together. "Raymond Burr" answers with Perry Mason and two of his films, none carrying his name; "drama" answers with The Golden Girls and Murder She Wrote. It is a ranking rather than a filter, so a word common in titles gives those first. Two ways in: Home's Browse by Genre row now works -- those fifteen cards are bare words with no page behind them, and were opening nothing -- and any film or show has "Search the cast...". - A search of hundreds of results no longer arrives one page at a time. The first page says how many there are, so the rest are fetched at once: a genre word matching 447 titles was 28 round trips in sequence before anything was drawn. - A cast written as prose is read as names. Most pages send a plain list, but some send "Starring Marlon Brand, Karl Malden and Katy Jurado", which split on commas alone gave a cast whose first member was "Starring Marlon Brand" and whose last was "and Katy Jurado". - A title's page says whether it is already a favourite, so the right verb is shown there rather than both. - Recording reaches beyond the guide. 1803 of the captured cards say they may be recorded -- films and channels among them -- and each names the form to use, which is not the one a guide airing names. The card's own form code is what gets asked for. - A title opened from Information can be favourited from there too; its play button had no context menu at all. - "More like this" on any film or show's context menu, and "Go to show" on a guide airing that belongs to a series -- the airing's overlay is the only thing that names the show it came from. - The guide carries descriptions, cast, artwork, episode numbers and certificates. The schedule endpoint sends a title and two times per airing and nothing else; everything readable is in each airing's overlay, fetched the same way and under the same setting as a listing's. - Continue Watching resumes. The service sends how far in you got as a fraction of the running time, and it was being read and thrown away, so that row restarted everything from the beginning. - A guide row for something not yet airing no longer fills the log with "InputStream: Error opening,". Those rows had an empty url, which Kodi treats as something to open rather than as inert; selecting one now says what it is and when it is on. - A lapsed session signs in once, not once per thread. Listings are fetched on a pool, so an expiry mid-listing would have had a dozen threads sign in at the same time, each invalidating the one before. - A film and a series describe themselves differently and both are now read correctly: a series has a description element and its subtitles are the episode on the air, while a film has no description element at all and its synopsis is the subtitle. Reading one rule for both left films blank and gave series their current episode's synopsis instead of their own. - Record an episode or a series, and stop or delete a recording, from the context menu on any guide airing. The service describes the choices and the addon echoes the chosen one back untouched, so it never has to know what the instruction strings mean. - The icon and fanart are Friendly TV's own logo, taken from the capture. - Live TV, the guide, and the service's own Home/Movies/TV/My Stuff pages. - Playback is Widevine DASH through InputStream Adaptive. Friendly TV's licence server takes a raw Widevine challenge and answers with raw licence bytes, which is exactly what ISA speaks, so there is no licence proxy in this addon and nothing listening on localhost. - Stream slots are handed back when playback stops. Friendly TV counts concurrent streams and only frees one when its poll key is posted back, so a client that never does locks the account out of its own subscription. - Optional IPTV Manager integration for Kodi's TV section.
